newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees 1997 cereal production at record levels.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees 1997 cereal production at record levels.

text.p: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday that its first forecast for 1997 world cereal production was 1,880 million tonnes, close to the record crop of the previous year.

"The first preliminary FAO forecast of world cereal production in 1997 is 1,880 million tonnes (including rice in milled terms), compared with 1,873 million tonnes in 1996," the Rome-based agency said in its Food Outlook report.
It said its estimates were "very tentative" and based on the condition of crops already in the ground, planting intentions and assuming normal weather conditions.
FAO said wheat output was provisionally forecast at 590 million tonnes, virtually unchanged from 1996 but above trend for the second year in succession.
It said output was forecast to rise in most of Asia, Europe and the former Soviet Union but this would be offset by lower crops forecast in North Africa, South America and Oceania.
The first forecast for 1997 global coarse grains output was 910 million tonnes, also virtually unchanged from 1996.
